stories.headline: OpenAI Closes Record $122B Funding Round at $852B Valuation, Reports $2B Monthly Revenue

key_facts.fact: OpenAI closed $122 billion in committed capital at an $852 billion post-money valuation, up from the $110 billion announced in February.
The round was anchored by Amazon ($50B), NVIDIA ($30B), SoftBank ($30B), and Microsoft, with co-leads including a16z, D.E. Shaw Ventures, MGX, and TPG.
OpenAI is now generating $2 billion in revenue per month, with enterprise accounting for more than 40% of revenue, on track to reach parity with consumer by end of 2026.
ChatGPT has over 900 million weekly active users and more than 50 million subscribers. Codex serves over 2 million weekly users, up 5x in three months.
OpenAI extended participation to retail investors for the first time, raising over $3 billion through bank channels, and will be included in ARK Invest ETFs.
SoftBank took out a $40 billion bridge loan from major financial institutions to fund its OpenAI investment.
OpenAI announced plans to build a 'unified AI superapp' combining ChatGPT, Codex, browsing, and agentic capabilities into one agent-first experience.

stories.headline: Anthropic Accidentally Leaks Claude Code's 512K-Line Source Code via Misconfigured npm Package

key_facts.fact: A 59.8 MB JavaScript source map file was inadvertently included in version 2.1.88 of the @anthropic-ai/claude-code npm package, exposing approximately 512,000 lines of TypeScript across ~1,900 files.
Anthropic confirmed the leak was 'a release packaging issue caused by human error, not a security breach' and said no sensitive customer data or credentials were exposed.
The leaked source revealed internal codenames: Capybara (Mythos) for a Claude 4.6 variant already at v8, Fennec for Opus 4.6, and Numbat as an unreleased model still in testing.
The code revealed a 'Self-Healing Memory' architecture, a three-layer memory system using lightweight pointers and on-demand topic files rather than traditional store-everything retrieval.
The source revealed a KAIROS feature flag (mentioned 150+ times) for an autonomous daemon mode that allows Claude Code to operate as an always-on background agent performing memory consolidation.
Claude Code has achieved an annualized recurring revenue of $2.5 billion, more than doubling since the beginning of the year, with enterprise adoption accounting for 80% of its revenue.
A clean-room Python reimplementation of the leaked code (claw-code) hit 44,500 GitHub stars within hours, raising questions about DMCA-proof derived works created by AI agents.

stories.headline: Google Warns Quantum Computers Could Break Crypto Encryption With 20x Fewer Qubits Than Expected

key_facts.fact: Google Quantum AI published a whitepaper showing elliptic curve cryptography protecting Bitcoin, Ethereum, and most cryptocurrencies could be broken with fewer than 500,000 physical qubits, down from roughly 9-10 million previously estimated — a 20-fold reduction.

The attack could be executed in minutes on a sufficiently powerful quantum machine. Under idealized conditions, a primed quantum computer has a roughly 41% probability of deriving a private key before a Bitcoin transaction is confirmed.

In an unprecedented move, Google chose not to publish the actual circuits, instead releasing a zero-knowledge proof that lets researchers verify the claims without reproducing the attack. This was developed in coordination with the US government.

The paper was co-authored with Justin Drake of the Ethereum Foundation and Dan Boneh of Stanford. It is the third major quantum threat paper in twelve months, following Gidney's RSA paper and Iceberg Quantum's Pinnacle architecture.
Google has set a 2029 internal deadline for its own post-quantum cryptography migration, a signal that carries particular weight given its own researchers produced these estimates.

stories.headline: OpenAI Ships Official Codex Plugin for Rival Anthropic's Claude Code

key_facts.fact: OpenAI open-sourced a plugin under Apache 2.0 that installs directly inside Anthropic's Claude Code, adding slash commands for code reviews, adversarial reviews, and task delegation to Codex.

The plugin provides six slash commands including /codex:review for standard reviews, /codex:adversarial-review for challenge reviews questioning implementation decisions, and /codex:rescue for full task delegation.

The move reflects competitive dynamics: Claude Code leads developer adoption with a $2.5B annualized run rate and 135,000 daily GitHub commits, while Codex has reached 1.6 million weekly active users.
A same-day vulnerability disclosure revealed a critical command injection flaw in Codex via manipulated branch names, potentially exposing GitHub OAuth tokens. OpenAI patched the issue.

stories.headline: North Korean Hackers Compromise Axios npm Package in Supply Chain Attack Affecting Millions

key_facts.fact: Malicious versions of the axios npm package (1.14.1 and 0.30.4) were published via a hijacked maintainer account, injecting a remote access trojan targeting macOS, Windows, and Linux. The package has over 300 million weekly downloads.
Google attributed the attack to UNC1069, a suspected North Korean financially-motivated threat actor that Google covered in a February blog post.
The malicious versions were live for approximately 2-4 hours before npm unpublished them. Cognition's Devin caught the attack for customers within one hour of injection.
The axios attack occurred hours before the Claude Code source leak, and the leaked Claude Code codebase itself was found to use the compromised axios package.

stories.headline: Google Launches Veo 3.1 Lite, Cuts AI Video Generation Costs by 50% as OpenAI Exits Sora

key_facts.fact: Google launched Veo 3.1 Lite, a cost-effective video generation model at less than 50% the cost of Veo 3.1 Fast, supporting both text-to-video and image-to-video at 720p or 1080p.
The model supports landscape (16:9) and portrait (9:16) aspect ratios with customizable duration at 4, 6, or 8 seconds. It is available today via the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.
The launch came following OpenAI's shutdown of its Sora video generation tool the previous week, with Google explicitly affirming its commitment to video generation tools.

stories.headline: AI Recruiting Startup Mercor Confirms Breach via LiteLLM Supply Chain Attack, Lapsus$ Claims 4TB Stolen

key_facts.fact: Mercor confirmed it was 'one of thousands of companies' affected by a supply chain attack on the open-source LiteLLM project, linked to hacking group TeamPCP.

Extortion group Lapsus$ claimed responsibility and shared samples including Slack data, ticketing data, and videos of conversations between Mercor's AI systems and contractors. They claim 939GB of source code and 4TB total data.
Mercor was valued at $10 billion following a $350 million Series C in October 2025 and works with OpenAI and Anthropic to train AI models by contracting domain experts.
The LiteLLM compromise involved malicious code in packages discovered last week; the library is downloaded millions of times per day according to security firm Snyk.

stories.headline: PrismML Emerges From Stealth With 1-Bit LLM That Fits 8B Parameters in 1.15GB, Runs on iPhone

key_facts.fact: PrismML, a Caltech-origin AI lab, emerged from stealth with $16.25M in SAFE and seed funding, claiming its 1-bit Bonsai 8B model achieves radical compression without sacrificing performance.

Bonsai 8B is a true end-to-end 1-bit model (embeddings, attention, MLP, and LM head all 1-bit) with 10.6x intelligence density per GB over Qwen3 8B, running at 40 tok/s on iPhone, 136 tok/s on M4 Pro, and 440 tok/s on RTX 4090.
PrismML claims 1-bit Bonsai 8B scores 1.06 intelligence per GB compared to 0.10/GB for the closest full-precision 8B model, representing a 10x improvement in intelligence density.

stories.headline: Oracle Cuts Up to 30,000 Jobs as It Redirects Spending to AI Data Centers

key_facts.fact: Oracle began notifying employees of a major layoff affecting an estimated 20,000 to 30,000 workers, roughly 12-18% of its 162,000-person global workforce.
Employees across the US, India, Canada, and Mexico received termination emails from 'Oracle Leadership' early on March 31. Oracle stock rose on the news.
The layoffs are tied to Oracle's ramp in AI data center capital expenditure to meet demand from OpenAI and other customers, with $553 billion in remaining performance obligations.

stories.headline: Salesforce Overhauls Slackbot With 30+ AI Features Including Meeting Transcription and Agent Mode

key_facts.fact: Salesforce announced more than 30 new AI capabilities for Slackbot, making it the most ambitious update since the Salesforce acquisition, transforming it into an AI agent for workplace tasks.
New features include meeting transcription, an operator mode that can complete multi-step tasks on the desktop, and deep integration with Salesforce's Agentforce platform.
Salesforce separately invested $330 million in Anthropic (~1% stake) after Microsoft blocked its attempted investment in OpenAI.

stories.headline: Liquid AI Releases LFM2.5-350M, a 350M-Parameter Model Trained on 28T Tokens for Edge Agentic Tasks

key_facts.fact: Liquid AI released LFM2.5-350M, a 350-million parameter model trained on 28 trillion tokens (80,000:1 token-to-parameter ratio), using a hybrid architecture of Linear Input-Varying Systems and Grouped Query Attention.

The model supports a 32K context window while running on extremely limited hardware: 169MB on Snapdragon NPU, 81MB on Snapdragon GPU, and 300MB on Raspberry Pi 5. On an H100, it reaches 40.4K output tokens per second.

The model scores 76.96 on IFEval (instruction following) and is optimized for tool use, function calling, and structured data extraction, though explicitly not recommended for complex coding or creative writing.

stories.headline: Hugging Face Releases TRL v1.0, Stable Post-Training Library With Async GRPO and Tool-Calling Support

key_facts.fact: Hugging Face released TRL v1.0, transitioning the post-training library from a research codebase into stable infrastructure for foundation model training, now handling approximately a significant portion of open-source RL training.

Key additions include Asynchronous GRPO (parallel rollouts eliminating idle GPU time), new RL trainers (VESPO, DPPO, SDPO), tool-calling support, and full OpenEnv integration for stateful multi-turn environment training.
The release enables developers to do the first successful GRPO fine-tune of models on live environments — demonstrated with Qwen3-1.7B on TextArena Wordle, taking win rate from 0% to 8%.

stories.headline: EU Institutions Ban Staff From Using AI-Generated Images and Videos in Official Communications

key_facts.fact: The European Union's three main institutions — the Commission, Parliament, and Council — banned staff from using fully AI-generated videos and images in official communications.
The ban comes amid growing scrutiny of the use of artificial intelligence and deepfakes, and applies to official messaging from EU institutional channels.

stories.headline: Perplexity AI Faces Class Action Alleging It Shared User Data With Meta and Google in Incognito Mode

key_facts.fact: Perplexity AI faces a proposed class action lawsuit alleging it shared users' personal data with Meta and Google even when users were in Incognito mode, violating California privacy laws.
The lawsuit alleges Perplexity used 'undetectable' tracking mechanisms to send personal information to Meta and Google without user consent, even in private browsing mode.

stories.headline: Yupp AI Shuts Down Less Than a Year After $33M Seed Led by a16z Crypto

key_facts.fact: Yupp, a crowdsourced AI model-picking service backed by $33M from a16z crypto's Chris Dixon, announced it is shutting down less than a year after launch, saying it 'didn't reach a strong enough product-market fit.'
Yupp had signed up 1.3 million users and allowed consumers to test and compare results from 800 AI models for free, generating crowdsourced preference data that AI labs would pay for.

The founders cited rapid AI model improvements as a key factor, noting the industry shifted to hiring specialty experts (PhDs) for reinforcement learning feedback rather than crowdsourced consumer data.

stories.headline: Baidu Robotaxi Fleet Freezes Across Wuhan in System Failure, Trapping Passengers on Highways

key_facts.fact: A suspected system failure caused dozens of Baidu Apollo Go robotaxis to freeze simultaneously across Wuhan, China on Tuesday, trapping passengers in vehicles and reportedly causing traffic disruptions and crashes on highways.

Some passengers were trapped for more than an hour, with one telling Wired it took 30 minutes to exit the vehicle. Wuhan traffic police said it was 'likely caused by a system malfunction' but still under investigation.
The incident occurred the same day Baidu Apollo Go and WeRide started driverless commercial operations in Dubai, highlighting the contrast between expansion ambitions and reliability concerns.

stories.headline: South Korea Chip Exports Hit Record $32.8B in March, Up 151% YoY, as Companies Front-Load Orders

key_facts.fact: South Korean chip exports more than doubled year-over-year to $32.84 billion in March 2026, up 151.4%, topping the $30 billion mark for the first time on record.
Total South Korean exports hit an all-time monthly high of $86.13 billion in March, up 48% YoY, surpassing the previous peak of $69.5 billion set in December 2025.
Companies rushed semiconductor orders due to fears of supply chain disruptions from the Middle East conflict threatening helium supplies critical to chip manufacturing.
Exports to China jumped 65% YoY to $16.5 billion driven by semiconductors, while exports to the US rose 47% to $16.34 billion.
Korea posted a trade surplus of $25.74 billion in March, extending its surplus streak to 14 consecutive months.

stories.headline: Nvidia and Tesla Turn to Samsung as TSMC 3nm Overload and 2nm Sellout Through 2028 Squeeze AI Chip Supply

key_facts.fact: TSMC's 3nm process has entered a state of 'overload' as chip designers and hyperscale cloud providers compete aggressively for limited capacity, forcing companies like Nvidia and Tesla to seek alternatives.
TSMC has fully booked its 2-nanometer chip capacity through 2028, with even its future Arizona Fab 4 (set for 2030 production) already reserved.
Samsung Foundry has secured chip orders from Tesla and Nvidia and may return to profitability this year, positioning itself as the only other player capable of producing 2nm chips.
TSMC held a 72% share of the pure-play foundry market in Q4, while Samsung ranked a distant second with 7%.

stories.headline: Samsung and AMD Sign MoU on HBM4 Memory Supply and Potential Foundry Cooperation for AI Chips

key_facts.fact: Samsung and AMD signed a memorandum of understanding covering HBM4 memory supply and possible future foundry cooperation for AI chips.
The agreement centers on Samsung providing HBM4 for AMD's MI455X AI GPUs, planned for its Helios rack-scale AI infrastructure platform.
The MoU also covers advanced DRAM for next-generation EPYC CPUs, linking AMD's GPU and CPU roadmaps under a single supply partnership.

stories.headline: Microsoft, Chevron, and Engine No. 1 Sign Exclusivity Deal for $7B Natural Gas Power Plant in West Texas

key_facts.fact: Microsoft, Chevron, and investment fund Engine No. 1 signed an exclusivity agreement for power generation and supply, tied to a proposed natural gas-fired power plant in West Texas.
The proposed facility has a projected cost of roughly $7 billion and would initially generate 2,500 megawatts of electricity to power a large data center campus.
Chevron and Engine No. 1 had already announced a partnership last year to build natural gas-based power plants next to data centers using GE Vernova turbines.
Chevron had previously said its first AI data center power project in West Texas targets start-up by 2027.

stories.headline: CoreWeave Closes $8.5B GPU-Backed Loan, First Investment-Grade Rated GPU Financing

key_facts.fact: CoreWeave closed an $8.5 billion delayed-draw term loan facility to expand its AI cloud platform, the first investment-grade rated GPU-backed financing.
CoreWeave can initially borrow about $7.5 billion, with an option to increase to $8.5 billion as data-center assets reach stable operating levels. The loan matures in March 2032.
The facility was co-structured by Morgan Stanley and MUFG, with Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan as additional lead arrangers, anchored by Blackstone Credit & Insurance.
This brings CoreWeave's total equity and debt financing commitments in the past 12 months to about $28 billion. Stock jumped 12% on the news.

stories.headline: Grab and WeRide Launch Southeast Asia's First Driverless Ride Service in Singapore's Punggol District

key_facts.fact: WeRide and Grab officially commenced public operations for the Ai.R autonomous ride service in Singapore's Punggol residential district on March 31, making Grab Southeast Asia's first ride-hailing provider to offer a driverless service.
The Ai.R fleet has served more than 1,000 early riders and clocked over 30,000 km of autonomous mileage since a January 2026 trial phase.
The service uses WeRide's GXR and Robobus autonomous vehicle models, with 14 Grab driver-partners trained as certified Safety Operators riding onboard during the initial phase.
Rides are free until commercial service begins in mid-2026. The fleet operates weekdays 9:30 AM to 5:30 PM on two shuttle routes plus a 20-minute mini route.

stories.headline: Tesla Admits Its Robotaxis Are Sometimes Fully Driven by Remote Human Operators

key_facts.fact: In a letter to Senator Ed Markey, Tesla disclosed that its robotaxi remote operators are allowed to directly control vehicles, unlike six other AV companies (including Waymo and Zoox) that said their remote assistants do not directly control vehicles.
Tesla simultaneously expanded its unsupervised robotaxi geofence in Austin to roughly 245 square miles (12x its original 20 sq mi), but the unsupervised fleet consists of fewer than a dozen vehicles.
The total Austin fleet is roughly 37-42 vehicles, with the vast majority still carrying in-car safety monitors; 'unsupervised' vehicles are still remotely supervised by Tesla.
Waymo by comparison is delivering 500,000 paid fully driverless rides per week across 10 US cities, targeting 1 million weekly rides by year-end.

stories.headline: Constellation Asks FERC to Speed Up Three Mile Island Nuclear Restart After Grid Operator Flags 2031 Delay

key_facts.fact: Constellation Energy filed a request with FERC on Tuesday to transfer grid connection rights from its Eddystone gas-fired plant to Three Mile Island (renamed Crane Clean Energy Center) to speed up its restart timeline.

Grid operator PJM Interconnection gave initial feedback that Three Mile Island may not be able to connect to the electrical system until 2031, but Constellation says it still plans to restart by end of 2027.
The $1.6 billion Crane relaunch, first announced in 2024, is intended to deliver electricity to power Microsoft data centers.

stories.headline: Autonomous Military Ship Maker Saronic Raises $1.75B at $9.25B Valuation to Scale Navy Production

key_facts.fact: Saronic raised $1.75 billion in a Series D led by Kleiner Perkins, more than doubling its valuation to $9.25 billion from $4 billion in early 2025.
Saronic plans to build more than 20 autonomous ships per year by 2027 and is potentially building a new shipyard (Port Alpha) in Texas.
Saronic's main shipyard in Franklin, Louisiana is undergoing a $300 million expansion, with plans to quintuple production over the next 12 months.
The company makes six autonomous surface vessel iterations and signed a $392 million Navy contract last year. The Iran war and Strait of Hormuz bottleneck are driving demand.

stories.headline: Microsoft on Track to Invest $5.5B in Cloud and AI Infrastructure in Singapore Through 2029

key_facts.fact: Microsoft confirmed it is on track to invest $5.5 billion in cloud and AI infrastructure in Singapore through 2029.
The Singapore investment follows Microsoft's announcement of plans to invest over $1 billion in Thailand for AI and cloud infrastructure.

stories.headline: Dow Surges 1,125 Points in Best Day Since Spring on Iran De-Escalation Hopes

key_facts.fact: The Dow Jones surged 1,125 points (+2.5%), the S&P 500 jumped 2.9%, and the Nasdaq rallied 3.8% on Tuesday, the best day for all three since last spring.
Despite Tuesday's rally, the S&P 500 closed its worst quarter since summer 2022 with a 4.6% loss, and major indexes each lost about 5% in March alone.
Brent crude fell 3.2% to $103.97 after Iran's president said Iran has 'the necessary will to end the war' given certain requirements, and extended declines to below $100 on Wednesday.
On Wednesday, Asian markets surged: South Korea's Kospi rose as much as 9.1%, Japan's Nikkei gained 5.2%, and MSCI Asia ex-Japan logged its biggest one-day increase since November 2022.
The 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.31% from 4.44% at end of last week, while U.S. gasoline topped $4/gallon for the first time since 2022.
Europe's STOXX 600 surged 2.3% on Wednesday, on track for its biggest daily jump in a year, led by travel stocks up 4%.

stories.headline: Iran's IRGC Warns 18 US Tech Companies Including Apple and Google Are Targets Starting April 1

key_facts.fact: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced it will target 18 major US technology companies operating in the Middle East starting Wednesday April 1, including Apple, Google, Microsoft, Nvidia, Tesla, Intel, and Boeing.
The IRGC stated: 'These companies should expect destruction of their facilities in response to each act of terror in Iran,' warning employees to stay away from workplaces.
The IRGC framed the threat as retaliation for US assassination operations, stating: 'For every assassination, an American company will be destroyed.'
Trump dismissed the threat at the White House, telling reporters: 'With what? What did they threaten them with? BB guns? They don't have much left to threaten.'

stories.headline: Iran Drone Strikes Fully Laden Kuwaiti Oil Tanker Off Dubai, Most Significant Ship Attack in a Month

key_facts.fact: An Iranian drone hit the Al-Salmi, a fully laden Kuwait-flagged very large crude carrier, in Dubai port's anchorage zone just 31 nautical miles northwest of the emirate, starting a fire on board.
All 24 crew members were safe and the fire was extinguished with no oil leakage, according to the Dubai Media Office and Kuwait Petroleum Corp.
More than 400 ships of all types were in and around the anchorage where Al-Salmi was struck at the time of the attack.
The attack initially pushed WTI crude futures up nearly 4% toward $107/barrel before gains were pared later in the day on de-escalation signals.
Iran has near-total control of the Strait of Hormuz and has effectively closed it to all but a trickle of vessels, paralyzing energy shipments from the Persian Gulf.

stories.headline: Trump Says US Could End Iran War in 2-3 Weeks, Will Address Nation Wednesday

key_facts.fact: President Trump said the US could end its military campaign against Iran 'within two or three weeks,' and that Iran would not need to agree to any terms for the withdrawal to proceed.
Trump is scheduled to deliver a televised Address to the Nation on Wednesday at 9 PM ET to provide an update on the situation with Iran.
Iranian President Pezeshkian stated Iran is open to ending hostilities but requires formal security guarantees against future attacks.
The Wall Street Journal reported the UAE is lobbying for a UN Security Council resolution to authorize military action to reopen the Strait of Hormuz by force.
CENTCOM said US forces struck Iranian underground military sites with precision munitions, and the IDF killed Mahdi Vafaei, head of the IRGC Quds Force Lebanon Corps Engineering Branch.
US Secretary of State Rubio said Washington will have to reexamine its relations with NATO after the Iran war ends.

stories.headline: EU Considers Reviving 2022 Energy Crisis Measures as Iran War Disrupts Markets

key_facts.fact: EU Energy Commissioner Dan Jorgensen said the bloc is considering reviving measures used in 2022 during Russia's gas cuts, including gas price caps and windfall profit taxes, to address disruption from the Iran war.
Jorgensen warned the disruption 'will not be short' even if peace comes soon, because 'energy infrastructure in the region has been ruined by war.'
European gas prices have risen more than 70% since the US-Israeli war with Iran began on February 28. EU inflation accelerated to 2.5% in March from 1.9% in February.

The EU's immediate concern is jet fuel and diesel supply: the last kerosene shipments from the Strait of Hormuz are due to arrive around April 10, after which Europe faces potential localized shortages.
Jorgensen asked EU governments to delay non-emergency refinery maintenance to keep oil product supplies flowing.

stories.headline: Eli Lilly to Acquire Centessa Pharmaceuticals for Up to $7.8B in Sleep Disorder Bet

key_facts.fact: Eli Lilly announced it will acquire Centessa Pharmaceuticals, which is developing treatments for excessive daytime sleepiness and neurological conditions, for approximately $6.3 billion upfront with up to $7.8 billion if certain milestones are met.
Centessa's stock soared 44% on the announcement, while Eli Lilly rose 3.7%.
The deal expands Lilly's neuroscience pipeline with sleep-wake treatments, a fast-growing therapeutic area.

stories.headline: FDA Approves Corcept's Lifyorli for Platinum-Resistant Ovarian Cancer, First Selective SGRA

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Lifyorli (relacorilant) in combination with nab-paclitaxel for adults with platinum-resistant epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer, making it the first FDA-approved selective glucocorticoid receptor antagonist.

In the pivotal ROSELLA trial, patients treated with Lifyorli plus nab-paclitaxel experienced a 35% reduction in risk of death compared to nab-paclitaxel alone, with median overall survival of 16.0 months vs 11.9 months.
Patients also saw a 30% reduction in risk of disease progression as assessed by blinded independent central review.
Corcept CEO Dr. Joseph Belanoff said the approval demonstrates the potential of cortisol modulation in oncology.

stories.headline: Autonomous Warship Startup Saronic Raises $1.75B at $9.25B Valuation for Naval Fleet

key_facts.fact: Saronic raised $1.75 billion in Series D funding led by Kleiner Perkins, more than doubling its valuation to $9.25 billion from $4 billion after a $600 million raise in early 2025.
Saronic plans to build more than 20 autonomous ships per year by 2027 and is potentially building a new shipyard called 'Port Alpha' in Texas.
The company's main shipyard in Franklin, Louisiana is undergoing a $300 million expansion, and Saronic says it is on pace to quintuple production there over the next 12 months.
Saronic last year signed a $392 million Navy contract. The Iran war and Strait of Hormuz bottleneck are driving urgent demand for unmanned naval systems.
CEO Dino Mavrookas said: 'We're seeing a real shift in demand towards unmanned systems that can be delivered at scale and at a fraction of the price point of traditional vessels.'
